claims.claim: The game features base building, PvP loops, and item gathering alongside server wipes.

citations.review_text: Rust is still one of the most intense survival games out there. The base building and PvP loop is addictive, and the constant risk of losing everything keeps it interesting.It’s rough on new players though. You’ll get killed a lot and raided if you’re not careful. Worth it if you can handle the losses, but it’s not casual-friendly.Solid game if you know what you’re getting into.

I haven’t played this game for very long, but I can still share my opinion.

Rust is an exciting survival game with beautiful graphics, a huge variety of items, and plenty of structures to explore and build. It’s best to play with friends because you’ll have a better chance of surviving together

But what about the survival aspect? The game can be quite challenging, but with the help of a few tutorials, you can learn the basics and get better at it

I highly recommend it!

Rust is neat. It's a one of a kind, If you like slaving to get a shit ton of guns, ammo, and other things, and have it wiped and restart at the end of the week, or month, this is your game. I think it's fun to kill people, steal their shit, and kill them again with their shit. It's also funny to hear my friends get pissed off when someone else does that to them.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience issues with customer support refusing to overturn permanent bans incurred after account hijacking.

citations.review_text:
Great Game Terrible Customer Support – Permanently Banned After My Account Was Hijacked

First of all, I want to say that Rust is genuinely a great game. I had a lot of fun playing it, made some great memories and really enjoyed my time in the game. My negative review isn't about the gameplay. It's about the absolutely disappointing customer support.

I stopped playing Rust a while ago and sometime later my Steam account got hijacked. After recovering my account I suddenly received a notification saying I had been permanently banned from Rust.

I contacted Rust support and explained everything, including the fact that someone else had gained access to my Steam account. But their response was basically that it didn't matter who was using my account They couldn't help me

Seriously? I understand that cheating is a serious problem and that developers need to protect their games. But what about players whose accounts get stolen? Are we just supposed to accept losing access to a game we paid for, even when someone else may have been responsible?

What disappointed me the most wasn't even the permanent ban. It was the complete lack of understanding or meaningful assistance from their support team

Rust is an amazing game, and I genuinely had a lot of fun playing it. But in my experience its customer support is among the worst I've ever dealt with

I never thought I'd be writing a negative review for a game I actually loved playing

Great game. Great memories. Terrible support experience

I wish things had ended differently.

Well, sh*t. What can I say? I would love to leave a 5 star review talk about this, talk about that, how much fun the game is, and how its basically a great training simulator for future psychopaths.

Except I can't really do that now, because my Steam account that I thought was secure with the Steam Guard got hacked, and the POS played all of one minute of Rust to get me permanently f***ing banned. Permanently.

What kind of absolute bulls**t is that? There is zero system in place to actually prove you were hacked and get unbanned. Their official response to being hacked is basically, it's your account, your responsibility,  and they simply don't give a f**k. Lol I guess I'm just not famous enough to get my account back.

And to make things even worse, now Steam literally advertises on my profile for the whole world to see that I'm a cheater.

But hey, don't worry, there's light at the end of the tunnel! They informed me that in just eight months—if I am not caught trying to get around the band, I am more than welcome to rebuy the game and make a new account and be able to play again lol.
How gracious of them to do that. Because, you know, I haven't already paid for the game. 
And for the record I wouldn't even know how to f**king cheat nor want too. 
And a big thumbs down to Steam for advertising that I'm a cheater when they can plainly see it wasnt me. Not cool Steam not cool.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game suffers from poor technical performance, including lagging, freezing, blurry visuals, and struggling to maintain high frame rates on capable hardware.

citations.review_text: Rust scratches an itch that no other PvP game can. I genuinely love playing this game, but it desperately needs another serious performance overhaul. It's honestly amazing how a game that's been around for this long still struggles to push past 60–100 FPS on most servers unless you're running a newer CPU or one with 3D V-Cache. I can play plenty of other modern titles and comfortably push 150–200+ FPS, yet Rust is one of the only games I play where I'm lucky to consistently break 120 FPS. And apparently, because my CPU doesn't have that magical "3D cache," I'm just out of luck.What's even more frustrating is that it feels like nearly every major update makes performance progressively worse. I understand Rust is a demanding game, especially with large maps, massive player counts, and player-built structures, but at some point, optimization needs to become a bigger priority.I'm not expecting 300+ FPS on a populated server, but I also don't think it's unreasonable to expect consistently good performance on hardware that's still more than capable of running modern games.Please, Face punch, give Rust the performance overhaul it desperately needs. I'd love to enjoy this game without having to sell my organs on the black market just to afford a new motherboard, ram and CPU.I love Rust, but I shouldn't need to build an entirely new PC every few years just to keep up with its declining performance. (This is also the reason I don't have more hours because my performance is so unbelievably terrible that it makes it really unfun to play)

Initially fun, but you get burned over and over by people who have a bunch of time and break into your base and steal and raid all your stuff, that you've spent hours collecting.  Then make it so you can't get back into your own base.  There aren't different levels of servers that I've found to play with like minded players.  Put a few days in this, and was burned every time, leaving me with nothing, just dead days.  Frustrating for different player types.  Also lags severely, freezes and blurry.  Running Nvidia 5070 laptop. 
 Overall not a good experience.  To much PvP for my type of gaming. PvP is all about this game, even on "Care Bare" servers, where all I try to do is collect resorses and expand base. Will be giving this one up, regretting loosing so many hours for nothing.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game receives monthly content updates that add new weapons, areas to explore, and keep the experience fresh.

citations.review_text:
This is a game you play when you have no job or no school. You can't have a life.

The combat system is amazing and so is the exploring. 

When it comes to customization, I really love the skins. ESPECIALLY the partnerships they do for free skins. 

This game has lots and lots of updates and is very well maintained. Always adding new spots to explore or weapons to try. 

It is a very unique game where you can raid/kill other players or team up with them, which is fun. But when you get to understanding the types of people that are playing, you'll soon realize that you're mostly gonna get betrayed, unless you betray them first.

To get basically anywhere, you'll need to grind A LOT. Which I don't even recommend because you'll probably wake up the next day with nothing. If I were you, I would watch a youtube video to understand and enjoy what the game is about. Other than that, not worth the time.
New content monthly keeps it fresh. I got into this game super late but loving it.
